title: Nano-Enabled Molecular Surveillance of Plant Health: Emerging Biosensors for Stress and Disease Detection
content: Plant health is a fundamental factor that determines agricultural productivity. Climate change has dramatically intensified both biotic and abiotic stresses affecting crops, leading to reduced crop quality and yield. Furthermore, traditional diagnostics often reveal stress only after visual indicators are present and irreversible damage has occurred. Culture-based techniques and molecular methods such as PCR and ELISA are precise, but they are oftentimes laborious, requiring complex equipment and may not be highly sensitive or specific. Nanosensors, which combine nanomaterials with biological recognition elements, offer high sensitivity, specificity and portability for early detection. This review describes their principles and components, including the analyte, bioreceptor, transducer, and signal processor. It also examines their applications in detecting fungal, viral, and bacterial pathogens, as well as abiotic stress markers. A multiplex system that can detect sensors simultaneously plays a significant role in pre symptomatic diagnosis. The review also discusses the use of nanobiosensors in combination with machine learning, wireless sensor networks, wearable plant sensors and smartphone applications as the potential basis for smart agriculture. Lastly, it addresses barriers for deployment in the fields such as variability of crops, cost, nanotoxicity, sustainability, accessibility of farmers or poor infrastructure and lack of regulatory standards in the future.
